title: Leased out your excavator: can it be confiscated?

scenes.dialogue: Advocates, if you lease out your excavator and it is used to dump waste, can the authorities confiscate it from you, the registered owner?
The owner says the lease made the lessee alone liable. It says the machine was seized on private land, while not in use. So is the confiscation lawful?
Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On twenty third October, twenty twenty six, Honourable Justice M A Abdul Hakhim of the Kerala High Court ruled.

scenes.dialogue: In August twenty twenty five, the Pulikkal Panchayat seized a soil excavator, alleging it was used to dump waste in an abandoned quarry.
scenes.shown: In August 2025, the Pulikkal Panchayat seized a soil excavator, alleging it was used to dump waste in an abandoned quarry.

scenes.dialogue: The Sub Collector confiscated it under Section Two Nineteen U of the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, to be auctioned, with the money going to the Panchayat.
scenes.shown: The Sub Collector confiscated it under Section 219U of the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, to be auctioned, with the money going to the Panchayat.

scenes.dialogue: The owner, a partnership firm, filed a writ petition. It relied on a lease saying the lessee alone would bear any penalty for the machine's use.
It argued the section needs a vehicle carrying waste on a public road, or returning after use. The State said the owner cannot hide behind a lease.

scenes.dialogue: Finally, what did the High Court decide? A vehicle returning after the offence can be seized even off a public road, and parking at the spot counts as return.
The plain paper agreement was not a lease deed. Even if it were, the owner took no reasonable care. The confiscation stood; the petition was dismissed.
